scene: SKIP: caring about a difference is an unspoken change of attitude, not an action; a comparison of two objects reads as vergelijken and two framed pictures as verschillen, so no honest single mark is left at this level.

SKIP: the literal sense would be lifting one corner of a heavy object, which is the same raised object as tillen and barely differs from pakken; the figurative sense of lifting a restriction has no picturable action at all.

one adult stands at a kitchen worktop with eyes closed, lips and tongue just taking the tip of a spoon that half rises out of a steaming pan; the other hand is cupped underneath to catch a drip. The face shows the taste arriving and nobody else is in the room.
must: lips touching a raised spoon above a steaming pan.
avoid: the spoon tipped fully into an open mouth and the head back (eten); a hand fanning the air above the pan (ruiken); a thumbs up held beside a plate; a nod of the head (keuren); a full plate held up to the viewer.
alt: Een volwassene heeft de ogen dicht en de lippen raken net de lepel boven een dampende pan.

scene: SKIP: appreciation is an inner judgement; two hands pressed to the heart read as houden van and a raised thumb reads as goedkeuren, so the card would be the picture of another verb.
close up on two pairs of hands: an officer's hands close a pair of handcuffs round two wrists held out together; the officer's sleeve shows a plain cuff band, and nothing else is in the frame.
must: handcuffs closing round two wrists held out together.
avoid: one adult sitting behind a high wooden desk (rechtspreken); two adults in a fist fight (vechten); one hand pulling another person by the arm (wegsturen); a handshake between two adults (afspreken); bars or a prison cell.
alt: Een agent sluit handboeien om twee polsen die naar voren worden gehouden.

scene: SKIP: ending is abstract; the zipper scene reads as dichtdoen (review M9).

one adult hands over a key on a plain round ring and a folded lease to a second adult whose open hand is already closing on the key; the second adult stands on a doorstep inside the door frame, and a suitcase waits on the step below. Both look at the key.
must: key and lease passing between two pairs of hands at a front door.
avoid: coins pushed across a shop counter (betalen); two adults shaking hands with nothing in them (afspreken); a suitcase alone in an empty room; a sign hanging from a door; the key held up in triumph (vinden).
alt: Bij een voordeur geeft iemand een sleutel en een gevouwen contract aan een nieuwkomer met een koffer.

scene: one adult drops a single coin into the slot of a ceramic piggy bank held steady in the other hand, the coin standing in mid-air a finger’s width above the slot; a small tin of coins stands closed beside it and no shop counter is in the frame.
must: one coin halfway down into the slot of a piggy bank.
avoid: coins pushed across a counter (betalen); a coin held up close to one eye; a piggy bank smashed open; a purse held tight to the chest (houden); banknotes fanned out like a prize.
alt: Iemand laat een muntje net boven de gleuf van een aardewerken varkentje zakken.

scene: SKIP: the score sense needs a diploma or a number and the travel sense is reaching a place, which is aankomen; a raised certificate would also read as presenteren, and nothing in a frame marks out what has been achieved.

SKIP: experience is an inner event spread over time, so it can only be drawn as a face in the middle of something happening, and that face reads as schrikken or genieten; there is no single picturable action.
SKIP: realising something is a silent change of understanding; the only marks are the thought bubble or the lightbulb, and both are A1 conventions that may not be used on this page.
SKIP: taking advantage of something has no honest single action; a person keeping a gift or a discount is the picture of krijgen or kopen, and an upward arrow is a symbol this level does not allow.

SKIP: promoting is the act of advertising, so it would be the picture of reclame maken; the literal other sense, moving a pawn up a board, needs a whole game laid out in the frame, which no learner reads at a glance.

one adult holds up one flat palm towards a second adult who is walking towards the edge of a cliff with eyes fixed ahead; the first adult’s mouth is open mid-shout and the raised arm stretches out. The second adult is one stride from the drop.
must: a raised flat palm and a shout stopping a walker at the cliff edge.
avoid: a red triangle on a stick beside the path (verbieden); a hand chopping the air near a phone (onderbreken); a finger wagging in another person’s face (berispen); a door held shut; a siren with nobody present.
alt: Een volwassene steekt een open hand op naar iemand die bijna over de rand van een klif stapt.

scene: SKIP: a promise of certainty is abstract; the only marks are a seal, a signed contract or a handshake, and those read as ondertekenen or afspreken, while a guarantee card has no picturable action at all.
SKIP: denying is saying no to a claim, so the picture needs two speakers and a speech bubble, which is praten; a head shake alone is the same mark as weigeren and does not say what is denied.
SKIP: caring is many actions, and each single moment is another card: verbinden, voeren, wassen (review M8).

one adult stands at the tiller of a small sailing boat and holds the mainsheet taut with the other hand; the wind has the big white sail curved out to one side and the hull is heeled over, a white spray at the bow. The boat sits on open water, not in a harbour.
must: a sail filled by the wind and one hand on the tiller.
avoid: an adult rowing with both oars (roeien); a motorboat with no sail; a ship’s wheel turned by two hands on a big deck; a person standing on a dock with a suitcase (reizen); a flag on a pole (zwaaien).
alt: Een volwassene staat aan het roer van een bootje; de wind bolt het grote witte doek aan de mast.

scene: SKIP: judging is inner; a balance is the convention of wegen and a mark sheet needs text (review M9).

one adult stands holding an open book with the pages fanned half turned, one hand caught in the very act of turning a leaf, and the eyes fixed on the lower page; the book is held up clear of the body, and there is no chair, no table and nobody else.
must: a hand turning one page of a book held open in the other.
avoid: a finger running down a column of text (lezen); a thumb pressed to a tablet (typen); a closed book pressed to the chest (houden); a hand smoothing a folder of loose sheets.
alt: Iemand houdt een boek open en slaat met de vrije hand een bladzijde om.

scene: SKIP: having something at one’s disposal is a state, not an action; an open cupboard or a held-out bunch of keys reads as hebben or pakken and says nothing about who may use what.

one adult stands beside a tall flip chart with one open palm laid flat against the board and the other arm sweeping up towards its top; the flip chart pages are blank, and one adult sits facing the board with their heads up and eyes on it. No lettering on the board.
must: one open palm held flat on a flip chart facing an audience.
avoid: a trophy held up in both hands (winnen); a sheet of paper handed over (geven); a shopkeeper turning a price sign (kosten); two adults shaking hands (afspreken).
alt: Een spreker legt een open hand op een leeg flipovervel en wijst met de andere arm naar boven.

scene: one adult stands at a wooden easel and lays a loaded brush on the canvas, the bristles just touching the wet paint; a paint pot and rags sit on a table at hand, and the other hand holds a palette with three blobs of colour. The canvas shows only broad strokes.
must: a brush touching wet paint on a canvas on an easel.
avoid: a pencil on a sheet of paper (tekenen); a roller on a long wall; a camera held up to the eye (fotograferen); a pen and a signature; a brush emptying into a pot.
alt: Een volwassene staat aan een ezel en zet de kwast op het doek, naast potten verf.

scene: two hands seen from above over a laptop keyboard, close up, one finger striking a key and the other fingers raised mid-move; only the hands and the keys fill the frame, and no screen and no person show.
must: fingers caught mid-strike on keys, close up.
avoid: a pen on paper (schrijven); a whole person at a desk with a laptop (werken); a finger on a phone screen (bellen); a page being turned (lezen).
alt: Twee handen boven een toetsenbord, van bovenaf gezien; één vinger raakt net een toets.

scene: SKIP: terminating is abstract; the phone hang-up reads as bellen or ophangen (review M9).
SKIP: working as it should is a state of a machine, shown by a running engine or a spinning motor, and a person checking it is testen or controleren; nothing in a single frame marks the difference.

one adult stands facing the viewer and brings both open palms together in front of the chest at the very moment of contact, fingers spread, elbows out; a second adult a metre away watches with a smile. There is no music, no stage and nothing to hold in either hand.
must: two flat palms meeting in the air in front of the chest.
avoid: one palm tapping a table top; a handshake between two people (afspreken); arms raised in the air with open mouths (juichen); a fist thumped on a door (kloppen).
alt: Een volwassene slaat de platte handen tegen elkaar vlak voor de borst.

scene: SKIP: identification is checking one thing against another, which reads as vergelijken; the only other marks are a fingerprint or an identity card, and an identity card needs writing on it.
SKIP: forming a row is an arrangement of people at rest, so it is the same picture as staan in a line; the sense of raking row on row, as of soil or text, has no single picturable action.
SKIP: combining is putting two things together, which is the picture of mengen; two unlike objects on one table would need a before and after to say that they have been united.
SKIP: inspiration is an inner spark; the only marks are the lightbulb or a rising arrow, and both are conventions this page may not use, while a person gazing at a painting is only kijken.
SKIP: publishing is abstract and needs printed text to read (review M9).

one adult shrinks on a chair while a second adult stands over them with one pointing finger raised and the head lowered towards the first; the seated adult’s arms are pulled in and their eyes are down. Both adults, and no parent or child is shown, and no belt or cane.
must: one raised pointing finger above a person sitting down.
avoid: a police officer with handcuffs (arresteren); a cane or a belt raised in the air; an open hand swung at a face (slaan); two adults in a fist fight (vechten); a locked cell door.
alt: Iemand zit ineengezakt op een stoel terwijl een staande volwassene een vinger op hen richt.

scene: SKIP: lengthening is a before and after, which one frame cannot show (review M9).

SKIP: filling a container is the concrete picture, but it appears as a hand pouring water into a glass, which is the picture of inschenken, while the figurative sense, fulfilling a duty or a promise, has no single action.

SKIP: maintaining or enforcing is an ongoing duty, so the only picture is an officer standing guard, which is staan and already the picture of other verbs; the literal sense, keeping a thing intact, is hebben.

SKIP: repeating is the same action done twice, so it needs two frames or a caption; a teacher with a raised finger is onderwijzen, and a raised hand with a fist would be a symbol this page does not allow.

SKIP: testing is another person’s judgement of a product or a pupil, which is the picture of beoordelen or keuren; a finger tapping keys on a keyboard is the separate verb typen, so no distinct mark is left.

one adult reaches into a brick oven with a cloth-wrapped hand and turns a loaf with the other hand, eyes narrowed; the crust nearest one end is blackened and a thin curl of smoke rises from it. The withdrawn hand is drawn back from the heat.
must: a blackened loaf with smoke rising from an oven.
avoid: a finger held under a cold tap (afkoelen); a candle burning upright on a table; a pot boiling over (koken); a person asleep on a beach; a whole plate of burnt food shown to the viewer.
alt: Iemand draait een brood in de oven; aan een kant is de korst zwart en stijgt rook op.

scene: one adult cuts a loaf in two on a board with a bread knife, and one half slides onto a plate held out by a second adult; only these two figures are in the picture.
must: a loaf cut in two with one half going onto an outstretched plate.
avoid: one adult handing a whole loaf to a second (geven); a shopkeeper taking coins (betalen); two adults each holding an end of a loaf (delen); a tray of drinks set down in front of a group.
alt: Iemand snijdt een brood doormidden en schuift een helft op het bord van een wachtende.

scene: SKIP: same drawing as sturen, an envelope at a postbox (review M8).

one adult stands behind a low counter and brings a round rubber stamp down onto a closed folder, the stamp’s base a finger’s width above the cover; a second folder already stamped with a dark ring lies beside it, and a stack of blank sheets waits at hand.
must: one rubber stamp pressing down on a folder at a counter.
avoid: an ink pad beside a pile of envelopes (posten); a hand held up showing a thumb print (identificeren); a pen on a form (schrijven); a price sign on a shelf (kosten); a laptop (typen).
alt: Iemand achter een balie drukt een ronde stempel op een map; een tweede map is al gestempeld.

scene: one adult stands at arm’s length from a stack of five loose bricks and frames them between a thumb and forefinger, one eye closed and the other fixed on the stack; the other arm hangs at the side. No measuring tool of any kind is in the frame.
must: one squeezed eye sizing up a stack between thumb and forefinger.
avoid: a tape measure or a ruler (meten); a calculator and loose coins; a balance with two pans (wegen); bare hands at the sides while looking away (kijken).
alt: Een volwassene houdt een stapel stenen tussen duim en wijsvinger, met een oog dicht.

scene: one adult stands with a garden hose held low and lets water run out along a narrow channel dug between two raised beds; the water lies in the channel as one dark ribbon flowing away in the direction the hand points. A bucket stands dry beside a spade.
must: water running as one ribbon along a dug channel.
avoid: a kettle on a stove (koken); a person staring at a tap; a barrel carried full in both arms (tillen); a row of wet paving stones (regen); a stream with nobody about.
alt: Een volwassene laat water uit een tuinslang door een gegraven geul lopen.

scene: SKIP: translating is between two languages, which needs text or flags in the artwork.
SKIP: insuring or assuring is abstract.
SKIP: fearing is inner; a frightened face is schrikken.
SKIP: preparing food is the picture of koken.

one adult leans into a large closed wooden crate on a bare floor with both palms flat against its side, the arms straight, the body slanted and the back foot braced; the crate has slid a hand's width, shown by a short scrape on the floor.
must: a whole body leaning into a crate with both palms flat on it.
avoid: a rope pulled towards the body (trekken); a drawer slid shut with one palm (schuiven); the crate lifted off the floor (tillen); a foot kicking the crate (schoppen).
alt: Iemand leunt met beide handpalmen tegen een grote kist; de achterste voet zet zich schrap.

scene: one adult stands and holds a closed bottle upright in one fist at chest height, moving it hard up and down; two short curved movement marks sit above and below the bottle, and the other hand hangs free.
must: a closed bottle in a fist with movement marks above and below it.
avoid: a bottle tipped to pour into a glass (gieten); a bottle at the lips (drinken); two people clasping hands (begroeten); a hand waving in the air (zwaaien).
alt: Iemand houdt een dichte fles stevig vast; korte boogjes boven en onder de fles tonen een beweging op en neer.

scene: SKIP: the common sense is figurative (talks that fail); a boat on a beach is a state, not an action.
SKIP: changing is veranderen in a formal register, and a before and after needs two frames.
SKIP: considering is inner.
SKIP: influencing is abstract.
SKIP: settling or establishing is abstract.
SKIP: mastering or controlling is abstract.
SKIP: a still picture cannot tell a balloon coming down from the stijgen balloon going up.

one adult reverses a small car into a gap between two cars standing at the kerb, seen from above and to the side; the driver's head is turned to look back over the shoulder, and the car is half into the gap. No sign and no lettering.
must: a car half reversed into a gap between two others at the kerb.
avoid: a car moving along an open road (rijden); a car at a fuel pump (tanken); a car with its bonnet open (repareren); a sign with a letter on it.
alt: Een auto rijdt achteruit een lege plek in tussen twee stilstaande auto's langs de stoep; de bestuurder kijkt achterom.

scene: SKIP: a strike is shown with placards, which need text; ceasing is abstract.
SKIP: granting is abstract.
